title: 2026 Race Recap – Western States 100
claims: The 2026 race was the 53rd Western States Endurance Run and was held on June 27-28, 2026.
Vincent Bouillard finished in 13:46:15 and became the first runner to complete the 100.2-mile course in under 14 hours.
The top three men and fourth-place Thomas Cardin broke the previous men's course record of 14:09 set by Jim Walmsley in 2019.

Jennifer Lichter took the lead at the Devil's Thumb aid station at mile 47 and finished in 15:28:06, beating Courtney Dauwalter's 2023 women's course record of 15:29:33 by a little more than a minute.
Riley Brady finished second in 15:42 and Marianne Hogan third in 15:51.
The race had 370 runners assembled in Olympic Valley and 322 finishers, an all-time high finish rate of 87 percent.
136 runners finished under 24 hours and earned silver belt buckles; other finishers under 30 hours received bronze belt buckles.
The final official finisher was Mike Smith in 29:58:31, just under the 30-hour cutoff.
The oldest female finisher was 64-year-old Stephanie Irving in 29:27.

Weather conditions included cool temperatures and high winds early, and the high temperature at the Auburn finish reached only 73 degrees F, nearly 20 degrees below the historical high average for June 27.
The event was first held in 1974 and is held on the last full weekend in June.
The course travels through the Sierra high country and the canyons of the American River on the ancestral lands of the Washoe and Nisenan tribes before finishing at Placer High School in Auburn.
